question: Why do hosted Ticket Booking runs lose tests in the first 10 to 17 s of the test phase, and is anything on our side the cause?
answer: It is a hosted-runner phenomenon at suite start, not our agent: in every affected run the failures are the first test of each initial Playwright worker (w0/w1) plus at most the first test of the first replacement worker; the replacement workers pass everything, faster than the first tests of clean runs. The same signature appears in three security-reproduction runs whose agent phase was one 25-token call writing a canned app, with no self-check browser and no launcher, so process teardown, self-check browser pressure and the 3000/3301 relay are excluded as necessary causes. Password hashing is excluded too: three clean 10/10 runs used scryptSync like the failing ones.

mechanism_notes.worker_restart: Playwright tears a worker down after a failed test and starts a new one; workerIndex 2+ are replacements. Every failure sits on w0, w1 or the first test of w2.
mechanism_notes.fast_fail: A login test that fails in about 1.2 s with "element(s) not found" is a page that died mid-expect: Frame._expect (playwright-core lib/server/frames.js) swallows a non-timeout exception such as a renderer crash and reports the last intermediate poll result instead. The next test on the replacement worker in both such runs reported "Target crashed" or hung 15 s.
mechanism_notes.evaluate_hang: locator.evaluate hanging after expect(control).toBeVisible() passed is a renderer or worker that stopped answering, not an application condition; tagName.toLowerCase() cannot block.
mechanism_notes.browser_fixture: The built-in browser fixture has timeout 0, so browser launch time is not charged to the first test.
mechanism_notes.trace_video: No attachments on any failed result, so the hosted runner records neither trace nor video; the local gate setting trace/video off matches.
